details:
**Lisa Murkowski**
Alaska's moderate Republican senator since 2002. In 2017, she joined Susan Collins and John McCain in voting against the "skinny repeal" of Obamacare. She won re-election in 2010 as a write-in candidate and again in 2022 under ranked-choice voting.

**Mary Peltola**
A Yup'ik Democrat who won the August 2022 special election for Alaska's only U.S. House seat, becoming the first Alaska Native in Congress. She campaigned as the "pro-fish" candidate and defeated Sarah Palin, among others.

**Don Young**
Alaska's Republican congressman from 1973 until his death in March 2022, making him the longest-serving Republican in House history. His death triggered the special election won by Mary Peltola.

**Top-four primary and ranked-choice voting**
A system Alaska voters adopted by ballot measure in 2020: all candidates run in a single nonpartisan primary, and the top four advance to a ranked-choice general election. The 2022 special election was the first to use it.

**Sarah Palin**
Governor of Alaska from 2006 to 2009 and John McCain's 2008 vice presidential running mate. She lost the 2022 House special election to Mary Peltola.

**Willow Project**
A large ConocoPhillips oil drilling project on Alaska's North Slope, in the National Petroleum Reserve. Biden approved it in 2023 after heavy lobbying from Alaska's congressional delegation, despite opposition from environmentalists.

**Dan Sullivan**
Alaska's Republican senator since 2015. He won his seat by defeating Democratic incumbent Mark Begich in 2014.

**Pebble Mine**
A proposed copper and gold mine near Bristol Bay, home to the world's largest sockeye salmon fishery. Dan Sullivan was criticized for accepting donations from Pebble Mine executives while claiming to oppose the project.

**Mark Begich**
Democratic senator from Alaska from 2009 to 2015, who lost his seat to Dan Sullivan. When he ran for governor in 2018, independent governor Bill Walker dropped out and endorsed him.

**Bill Walker**
The independent governor of Alaska from 2014 to 2018. He ended his re-election campaign and endorsed Democrat Mark Begich.

**Joe Miller and the 2010 write-in campaign**
Tea Party favorite Joe Miller defeated Lisa Murkowski in the 2010 Republican Senate primary. Murkowski then won the general election through a write-in campaign, the first successful Senate write-in since Strom Thurmond in 1954.

**Kelly Tshibaka**
A Trump-endorsed Republican who challenged Lisa Murkowski in 2022 under the new ranked-choice system. Murkowski won re-election.
